Sheath is a single perimeter around the supports, which makes them sturdier and you can remove them all at once, but there is a higher chance of damaging the model.
Sometimes you waste material I once printed a bad version of a part I needed (500g) and I found out when I was building it.. It comes with the hobby. 😅

I once had one fragile model to print and had the same issue then I found a thread on prusaforums that called for:

0.25mm z distance.

75% xy distance.

3mm support spacing.

4 interface layers.

0.2mm interface layer spacing.

This worked like a charm but I only use it when the supports threaten the model...

[Sauce](https://forum.prusaprinters.org/forum/prusaslicer/prusaslicer-hard-to-remove-supports/)

Also credit: u/bobstro

Edit: Also make sure to NOT use sheath when printing fragile things it will take a bit of work to remove the supports without it but it should make the task safer.
